newsitem.title: USA: Yazaki breaks ground on $61 mln U.S. headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Yazaki breaks ground on $61 mln U.S. headquarters.

text.p: Japanese auto parts maker Yazaki Corp said Wednesday it broke ground on $61 million headquarters building for its U.S. operations here.

The new headquarters for American Yazaki Corp will allow the company to consolidate other operations in the Detroit area. When the facility is completed, the privately held company's 28-acre southwest suburban Detroit campus will consist of three buildings.
"The establishment of this new facility will help us to better service our customers through improved communications and new technology," American Yazaki President Tetsuro Suzuki said in a statement.

Yazaki's major automotive products include vehicle wiring harnesses, instrument clusters and other components. It acquired Chrysler Corp's Acustar Electric Wiring Division in 1994 for $225 million and remains Chrysler's major supplier of wiring harnesses.
General Motors Corp on Wednesday settled a day-long strike at its wiring harness unit, Delphi Packard Electric Systems, in Warren, Ohio.
